title: A generic protocol for the affinity-purification of native macromolecular complexes from poxvirus-infected cells
protocol: Determine the viral infectivity by performing a plaque assay.
Prepare 10-fold dilutions of the virus stock.
Use these aliquots to infect cell monolayers.
Cover infected cells with agar or cellulose.
Incubate the samples for 2 days.
Stain and count the viral plaques to calculate the virus titer.
Select an insertion site without interfering with neighboring ORF expression.
Determine if the VACV protein of interest can be expressed as an N- or C-terminal FLAG/HA fusion protein based on its genome localization.
Insert the FLAG/HA tag at the 3′ end of the A24R ORF in VACV RNA polymerase subunit Rpo132.
Clone the FLAG/HA sequences and viral flanks 1 and 2 into the TDS vector.
Transfect the generated TDS vector into VACV infected cells to allow homologous recombination between flank 1 or flank 2 of the vector and the respective sequence in the VACV DNA.
Isolate recombinant VACV from step four by performing consecutive rounds of plaque purification.
Perform the first rounds of plaque purification in the presence of specific virus growth inhibitors that allow growth of recombinant viruses only.
Enrich recombinant VACV, which have incorporated the TDS vector and therefore express the gpt gene conferring resistance to the growth inhibitors.
Remove growth inhibitors and perform plaque purification.
Observe loss of selection markers (gpt and mCherry genes) by fluorescence microscopy.
Seed 0.25×10^6 CV-1 cells per well in 1 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS in a 12-well plate.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37°C in 5% CO2 until they reach a confluency of 80% (approximately 24 hours).
Thaw a virus aliquot and sonicate for 1 minute in a water bath sonicator at 4°C for at least three cycles with a 1-minute pause on ice between cycles.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions from 10^-1 to 10^-8 in 1 mL of DMEM medium with 2% FBS.
Remove medium from the 12-well plate.
Add 300 μL of viral suspension per well and incubate for 1 h at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Add 500 μL of 2.5% (w/v) CMC medium on top of each well and incubate the plate for 48 h at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Remove medium from each well.
Add 200 μL of crystal violet solution per well and incubate at 25°C for 2 h.
Remove crystal violet solution and wash with milli-Q water.
Dry plate and count plaques.
Use public databases, such as NCBI, for genome accession of the Western Reserve VACV strain or any other VACV strain.
Identify the transcription directions of the ORF to be tagged and its neighboring ORFs.
Localize the promoter near the start codon using consensus sequences or mapped data from reporter assays or next generation sequencing techniques.
Select an intergenic region as the insertion site where the neighboring gene has its 3′ end.
Design oligonucleotides containing the FLAG and HA sequences with a preceding ATG for N-terminal tagging.
Design oligonucleotides containing the FLAG and HA sequences with a terminal stop codon for C-terminal tagging.
Digest the empty TDS vector with ClaI and SalI.
Perform an infusion reaction with either the N- or C-terminal FLAG/HA oligonucleotides.
PCR-amplify the sequences upstream of the desired FLAG/HA insertion site using VACV genomic DNA as template.
PCR-amplify the sequences downstream of the desired FLAG/HA insertion site using VACV genomic DNA as template.
Ensure each amplified flank is approximately 500 nucleotides in length.
Digest the TDS vector generated with ClaI.
Perform an infusion reaction with the upstream flank PCR product.
Digest the plasmid with SalI.
Perform an infusion reaction with the flank 2 PCR product.
Verify the generated plasmid by sequencing using T7 promoter specific primer (5′ TTCGATATCAAGCTTATCGAT 3′).
Infect cells with wild-type virus.
Transfect cells with the TDS vector generated in a previous step.
Allow homologous recombination to occur via flank 1 or flank 2.
Seed 1×10^6 HEK293T cells per well in 2 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS in a 6-well plate.
Grow cells at 37°C until they reach 60%-80% confluency in a humidified incubator equilibrated with 5% CO2.
Dilute crude wild-type virus stock to a MOI of 0.05–0.1 in DMEM medium with 2% FBS.
Remove medium from cells.
Replace with 1 mL of virus inoculum per well and incubate in 5% CO2 at 37°C for 2 h.
Prepare the transfection reaction by diluting 3-4 ug of vector in 0.5 mL of Opti-MEM medium, 30 min before the end of the incubation time.
Add 7.5 μL of transfection reagent and incubate at 25°C for 20 min.
Aspirate virus inoculum from cells.
Replace with 1 mL of DMEM medium containing 10% FBS per well.
Add transfection mixture drop-by-drop to the wells.
Incubate at 37°C for 24–48 h.
Harvest cells using a disposable cell scraper.
Collect whole cell suspension in a sterile tube.
Snap-freeze the cell suspension in liquid nitrogen.
Incubate the frozen cell suspension in a water bath at 37°C until complete thawing.
Repeat steps involving snap-freezing and incubation for three consecutive cycles.
Store the virus-containing cell suspension at -80°C.
Test cell lines for mycoplasma contamination before usage.
Isolate recombinant VACV expressing FLAG/HA tagged viral protein of interest.
Perform 3 to 4 rounds of plaque purification in the presence of MPA, XT, and HXT.
Block synthesis of purine nucleotides with MPA.
Initiate alternative pathway for purine synthesis using XT and HXT as precursors.
Identify recombinant plaques by fluorescence microscopy.
Seed 2×10^5 BSC-1 cells per well in 2 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS in a 6-well plate.
Incubate cells at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Incubate BSC-1 cells with 2 mL of selection growth medium containing 1/400 volumes of 10 mg/mL MPA, 1/40 volumes of 10 mg/mL XT and 1/670 volumes of 10 mg/mL HXT for 16–24 hours prior to infection.
Thaw the cell suspension containing virus and sonicate it for 1 minute in a water bath sonicator at 4°C with three cycles, pausing on ice for 1 minute between cycles.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions of the cell suspension in DMEM medium with 2% FBS.
Remove media from BSC-1 cells and add 1 mL of the diluted cell suspension per well using either a 10^-1 or 10^-3 dilution.
Incubate cells for 1–2 hours at 37°C.
Remove inoculum and replace with 1 mL of a 1:1 mixture of 2% low melting point agarose and 2× MEM medium, containing MPA, XT and HXT.
Incubate infected cells at 37°C for 48 hours to allow VACV plaques to form.
Use a 200 μL pipet tip to pick single, mCherry-positive, clearly separated plaques and transfer into fresh tubes containing 0.5 mL of DMEM medium with 2% FBS.
Freeze – thaw each tube and sonicate as described in step 5, c.

Perform two or three rounds of plaque purification without selection: Repeat steps 5, a to 5, k at least three times without MPA, XT and HXT using the last selected mCherry-positive plaques as starting material.
Transfect the pRB21 plasmid into vRB12 infected cells.
Identify and isolate recombinant viruses based on their ability to form plaques.
Clone the FLAG/HA-tagged protein of interest into pRB21.
Digest the pRB21 vector with the desired restriction enzyme(s) present in the MCS.
Design oligonucleotides to amplify the entire gene of interest with an N- or C-terminal FLAG/HA tag for cloning into the pRB21 vector.
Amplify and clone the desired insert into the pRB21 vector.
Verify the generated plasmid by sequencing using the pRB21 sequencing primer.
Infect cells with vRB12 virus.
Transfect infected cells with the generated pRB21 vector construct.
Amplify the vRB21 strain using an MOI of 1 Pfu/cell or more.
Estimate virus titer by counting plaques on the 5th day post-infection.
Isolate recombinant VACV based on their ability to form large plaques within 2–3 days.
Seed 2×10^5 BSC-1 cells per well in 2 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS in a 6-well plate and incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Sonicate recombinant virus (1.5 × 10^7 Pfu) and infect BSC-1 cells with 150 μL of crude viral extract per well.
Aspirate medium and scrape cells in 500 μL PBS buffer after 48 h post-infection.
Transfer 400 μL of the suspension into a new tube.
Add 50 μL of 10× TEN buffer, 50 μL of 10% SDS, and 5 μL of 20 mg/mL of Proteinase K to the cell suspension.
Incubate at 56°C for at least 2 h.
Add 600 μL of Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl alcohol 25:24:1 to the mixture, vortex briefly.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g in a tabletop centrifuge for 10 min at 4°C.
Collect the aqueous phase and add an equal volume of Chloroform.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 16,000×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the aqueous phase into a new tube.
Add 1/10 v/v of 3M NaOAc (pH 5.2) to the aqueous phase.
Add 3 volumes of 99.8% EtOH to the mixture.
Incubate at least 30 min at -20°C.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g for 20 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Wash pellet with 1 mL of 80% EtOH.
Centrifuge samples at 5,600×g for 15 min.
Remove supernatant after washing step.
Dry DNA pellet for 30 min.
Resuspend dried DNA in approximately 30 μL of milliQ H2O.
Sequence DNA from 10 different plaques.
Seed 5–7×10^6 HeLa S3 cells per 145 cm² dish in 20 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS.
Remove the medium from dishes and add 9 mL of DMEM medium with 2% FBS.
Thaw the crude virus stock (108 Pfu/mL) and sonicate for 1 min in a water bath sonicator at 4°C, repeating for at least three cycles with a 1-minute pause on ice between each cycle.
Add 200 μL of thawed and sonicated crude virus stock to each plate.
Incubate cells at 37°C until the cytopathic effect becomes visible (approximately 2 days post-infection).
Remove medium from plates once cell lysis starts, cells round up, and get notably bigger.
Harvest cells with a cell scraper and pellet cells in a 50 mL Falcon tube at 1,800×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and re-suspend the pellet in 35 mL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.8).
Store the re-suspended pellet at −80°C if not immediately used; thaw it in a water bath at 37°C when needed for further steps.
Homogenize cell suspension with 40 strokes in a glass dounce homogenizer with a tight pestle.
Monitor the degree of cell homogenization with a light microscope.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 4°C and 1,800×g to remove cellular debris.
Transfer supernatant to a new Falcon tube.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 3–5 mL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.8).
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 4°C and 1,800×g.
Pool supernatants from steps 23 and 24.
Split pooled supernatants into 3–5×5 mL aliquots.
Sonicate each aliquot for 1 min in a water bath sonicator at 4°C with a 1 min pause on ice between cycles, repeating for three cycles.
Layer the suspension on top of a 36% sucrose cushion using 17 mL of sucrose solution per tube.
Centrifuge at 26,000×g for 2 h at 4°C.
Remove supernatant from tubes after centrifugation.
Re-suspend pellet in 1 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.8).
Determine virus titer by plaque assay.
Purify virus using sucrose cushion method.
Combine sucrose cushion purified virus on top of a 24%–40% sucrose gradient.
Centrifuge for 40 min at 26,000×g at 4°C.
Prepare a 24%–40% sucrose gradient by layering solutions manually and letting it seat for 12–18 h at 4°C.
Aspirate sucrose above the milky band containing virus.
Collect virus-containing fraction carefully with a sterile pipet.
Place collected virus in a sterile centrifuge tube.
Bring volume up to 30 mL with 1 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.8).
Centrifuge samples at 32,900×g for 1 hour at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of 1 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.8).
Sonicate the resuspended sample for 3 cycles at 4°C.
Split sonicated virus into smaller aliquots.
Store aliquoted samples at -80°C.
Seed HeLa S3 cells on 145 cm² dishes.
Incubate seeded cells for 72 hours at 37°C in a 5% CO₂ environment to achieve 90%-100% confluency.
Infect confluent HeLa S3 cells with recombinant VACV expressing Rpo132-HA/FLAG fusion protein.
Incubate infected cells for 24 hours after viral adsorption before starting the vRNAP complexes purification process.
Harvest cells by trypsinization once confluency is reached.
Count number of cells per plate using a cell counting chamber.
Remove medium from cells.
Add 9 mL of DMEM medium with 2% FBS to each dish.
Thaw an aliquot of the virus stock and sonicate before use.
Dilute the sonicated virus stock in DMEM medium with 2% FBS.
Add 1 mL of diluted virus stock to each dish.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 h.
Replace inoculum with 20 mL of DMEM medium with 10% FBS.
Incubate cells for 24–40 h at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Remove medium from infected cells.
Collect cells using a cell scraper.
Pool cell suspensions in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the pooled cell suspension at 1,800×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Equilibrate FLAG-agarose beads with lysis buffer.
Centrifuge beads at 2,054×g for 2 min at 4°C.
Remove buffer from the resin.
Wash beads twice with 10 bed volumes of Wash buffer.
Add Protease inhibitor cocktail to the lysis buffer.
Re-suspend cell pellet in 30 mL of lysis buffer.
Incubate sample on ice for 20 min.
Clear the lysate from cellular debris by centrifugation at 15,000×g for 20 min at 4°C.
Collect supernatant and incubate with equilibrated FLAG-agarose beads on a rotating wheel or on a rolling bar shaker for 3 h at 4°C.
Centrifuge beads at 2,054×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Wash beads 3 times with 10 bed volumes of wash buffer.
Equilibrate beads with elution buffer.
Wash beads once with 10 bed volumes of elution buffer without 3×-FLAG peptide.
Dilute 3×-FLAG peptide with elution buffer to 200 μg/mL.
Add one bed volume of diluted 3×-FLAG peptide to the beads.
Incubate sample for 12–18 hours at 4°C on a stirring wheel.
Collect eluate the next day.
Concentrate eluate to 100–200 μL using a Vivaspin 500 concentrator at 10,000×g and 4°C.
Load sample onto a 10%–30% sucrose density gradient.
Centrifuge at 165,000×g for 16 hours at 4°C.
Manually collect 200 μL fractions.
Analyze the protein composition of each fraction by separating on a 12% Bis-Tris denaturing polyacrylamide gel.
Store fractions at -80°C for up to several months.
Purify Rpo132-HA/FLAG-containing complexes from HeLa S3 infected cells using an anti-FLAG affinity column.
Separate the eluate on a 10%–30% sucrose density gradient.
Analyze fractions by Bis-Tris denaturing PAGE and visualize by silver staining.
Isolate vRNAP complexes mainly present in fraction 11 and 12 for core complexes, and in fraction 15, 16, and 17 for complete complexes.
Carry out the isolation of vRNAP complexes on ice or at 4°C after cell lysis.
